messages:
Mona: quick Q — we're about to ship a client that sets `X-Model-Version: 2026-03-01` to pin behavior for `/v1/generate`. What's the official server contract here? Should the server: honor exact version only, fallback to family-compatible variant, or return an error? Also what's the deprecation window for pinned versions?
Raj: short answer: for hosted/Dedicated we should honor exact model-version if it exists. If it doesn't exist we return 400 with an error payload and a helpful hint header (`X-Compatible-Versions`) rather than silently falling back. Silent fallback has caused regressions. Deprecation policy: we announce deprecations, keep versions available for 90 days after notice, and send 30/15/7 day reminders.
Kelsey: does that apply equally to Private installs? Customers might be running their own weights/versions.
Raj: Private deployments are customer-controlled. We still validate the header shape, but we allow a runtime config `allow_version_fallback: true` in private bundles so operators can opt into family fallbacks. Hosted/Dedicated: strict.
Mona: got it. One more: how should clients detect breaking changes in the *response shape*? E.g., a model adds a `safety_metadata` object or renames `tokens` -> `token_stream`.
Tim: we should avoid inventing lots of headers, but we do need an explicit signal. Two options: 1) use an `X-Response-Schema` response header indicating the schema version; 2) include `response_schema_version` in model metadata and surface it in headers. I'm leaning to the latter (metadata-driven).
Leah: ops/rollout note: we want automated canaries for shape changes. Proposal: require onboarding to include `response_schema_version` (semver-like: `1`, `1.1`). Runtime will emit `X-Response-Schema: 1.1` so clients can assert compatibility.
Kelsey: sounds good. SDKs should default to not pin response schema, only to assert it if the user opted into strict mode. Also, document the exact header names so SDKs can map them.
Mona: example flow in client: set `X-Model-Version` to pin weights. If server returns 400 with `code: model_not_found` and `X-Compatible-Versions: 2025-12-01,2026-02-10`, client shows a user-facing message: "Pinned model version unavailable — upgrade?" Agree?
Kelsey: yep. Also treat 400/model_not_found as non-retryable. Surface clean error.
Raj: adding specifics for implementers:
```
Request header: X-Model-Version: 2026-03-01
If exact model exists -> 200 (normal)
If not -> 400 {"error":"model_not_found","message":"Model version unavailable"}
Response header: X-Compatible-Versions: 2026-02-10,2025-12-01  # optional suggestions
Response header: X-Response-Schema: 1.1
```
Raj: deprecation timeline (draft): announce -> 90-day support window -> automatic reject after window. Communication channels: email to billing contacts, console banner, SDK telemetry pings that detect pinned usage.
Tim: playbook for breaking-change comms: 1) PR in repo with migration notes + example diffs, 2) create docs/migration guide, 3) open internal changelog + 90d notice, 4) optional gradual rollout with canary if the change only affects generated tokens not API surface.
Mona: who owns adding `response_schema_version` to the model onboarding flow? @Kelsey?
Kelsey: I can take onboarding pieces, will add a small UI field and require it in the model metadata manifest.
Mona: thanks — pinging @Kelsey for quick review on the client PR that adds `X-Model-Version` support.
Kelsey: will review tonight. Small nit for client impl: if server sends `X-Response-Schema` and it doesn't match the client's expected schema, log a warning AND surface a non-fatal error to the app so product can decide.
Leah: ops: we'll add a runtime metric `models.pinned.requests` and `models.pinned.errors` so we can track how many clients rely on pinned versions. Also will add alert if pinned error spikes after a deploy.
Raj: agreed. Action items: [1] Add `response_schema_version` requirement to onboarding docs (owner: Kelsey). [2] Runtime: 400 on missing exact version for hosted/dedicated (owner: Eng Runtime). [3] Docs: deprecation timeline + header semantics (owner: Docs). [4] SDKs: warning + opt-in strict schema checks (owner: DevEx). [5] Instrument telemetry for pinned usage (owner: Eng SRE). I'll create tickets for each.
deploy-bot: created ticket RDW-1198 "model-version header semantics + response schema" and doc stub at https://internal.redwood.dev/api-contracts/versioning
Mona: perfect. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Kelsey: noted, leaving a short review comment on the PR with tests for the 400 case and header parsing.
